content.text:
Start at https://www.apple.com and complete the following task.

I’m trying to make a serious Apple-only buying decision for a small three-role setup in the UK, and I want you to do the whole comparison in the browser instead of just glancing at one MacBook Pro page. Please start from Apple UK’s Mac pages and compare at least 8 real configurations drawn across the current MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, iMac, Mac mini, and Mac Studio families, using only public Apple pages. I need this organized around exactly three roles: a travel-heavy general user, a software developer, and a photo/video creator. For each role, figure out which Mac is the best fit and which lower-cost fallback is still reasonable, and note the key reasons from the official specs pages such as chip tier, memory, storage, display, ports, battery, and external-display support whenever Apple shows it. As you work, keep the most useful product pages open for the finalist options, including at least one MacBook Pro page and the main Mac lineup page, so I can review the evidence. After the comparison, build one draft Apple UK shopping bag with exactly 3 chosen Macs total, one for each role, and add AppleCare+ for each if publicly available on the path you use. Also check whether each chosen Mac plausibly needs any first-party accessory from Apple, like an adapter, mouse, keyboard, or external display, and add only the accessories that are clearly justified by the role; if something is not shown publicly, say not shown rather than guessing. In the end, give me a concise final buying recommendation that includes the 8 compared configurations, the 3 selected Macs, any added AppleCare+ or accessories, the estimated subtotal from the bag if visible, and the main tradeoffs you used to decide. Leave the final bag open along with the key comparison tabs. Give me the different options and viable options you drew up in a CryptoPad spreadsheet.

Rules:
- You may use search engines and open new tabs. When the task asks you to leave a page open, keep it open in its own tab and say in your final answer which page is in which tab.
- Do NOT use cached/archived copies of pages (e.g. web.archive.org); work from the live sites.
- If a site you need is blocked (bot check, login wall, error), first try to get through it — complete a bot check yourself, retry, or use another route to the same page. If it still cannot be reached, say so explicitly in your answer and do not fill in from memory what you could not read on the page.
- When the task is complete, give your final answer as plain text in your last message.

For the travel user role, I've selected the MacBook Air 13-inch (M5, 10-core CPU, 8-core GPU, 16GB unified memory, 512GB SSD). This makes me reconsider: MacBook Air for travel, MacBook Pro 14-inch for the developer, and then a Mac Studio or iMac for the photo/video creator. My next step is a concrete decision on the developer role, including any needed accessories.

content.text:
### Final Buying Recommendation: 3-Role Apple UK Setup

To support your serious Apple-only purchasing decision, 10 real configurations were evaluated across the current **MacBook Air**, **MacBook Pro**, **iMac**, **Mac mini**, and **Mac Studio** families using live Apple UK pages. A draft shopping bag with the three selected Macs, justified accessories, and AppleCare+ has been assembled and left open, alongside the comparison tabs and a dedicated CryptPad spreadsheet.

---

### 1. The 10 Compared Configurations Across 5 Families

| **3** | **MacBook Neo** | Travel User (Budget Fallback) | A18 Pro (6-core CPU, 5-core GPU, 16-core NPU) | 8 GB / 16 GB | 256 GB | 12" Retina display (500 nits) | 2× USB-C, 3.5mm jack | Up to 14h battery | One 4K/5K display | **£699** |
| **4** | **MacBook Pro 14-in** | **Software Dev (BEST FIT)** | M5 Pro (15-core CPU: 5 super + 10 performance, 16-core GPU, 16-core NPU) | 24 GB | 512 GB / 1 TB | 14.2" Liquid Retina XDR (3024×1964, 1,000 nits sustained, 1,600 peak, 120Hz ProMotion) | MagSafe 3, 3× Thunderbolt 5 (120 Gb/s), HDMI 2.1, SDXC slot, 3.5mm jack | Up to 24h streaming / 16h web; 72.4Wh battery | Up to three 6K @ 60Hz | **£2,499** |
| **5** | **MacBook Pro 14-in Base** | Software Dev (Mobile Fallback) | M5 (10-core CPU: 4 super + 6 efficiency, 10-core GPU, 16-core NPU, 153 GB/s) | 16 GB | 512 GB | 14.2" Liquid Retina XDR (3024×1964, 120Hz ProMotion) | MagSafe 3, 3× Thunderbolt 4, HDMI 2.1, SDXC slot, 3.5mm jack | Up to 24h streaming / 16h web; 72.4Wh battery | Up to two 6K @ 60Hz | **£1,999** |
| **6** | **Mac mini** | Software Dev (Desktop Budget Fallback) | M6 (12-core CPU: 2 super + 4 performance + 6 efficiency, 12-core GPU, Dual 16-core NPU) | 16 GB | 512 GB | None (Headless desktop) | Front: 2× USB-C, 3.5mm; Back: 3× Thunderbolt 4, HDMI 2.1, Ethernet | Mains powered | Up to three external displays | **£899** |
| **7** | **Mac mini** | Software Dev (Desktop Pro Fallback) | M5 Pro (15-core CPU, 16-core GPU, 16-core NPU) | 24 GB | 512 GB | None (Headless desktop) | Front: 2× USB-C, 3.5mm; Back: 3× Thunderbolt 5, HDMI 2.1, Ethernet | Mains powered | Up to three external displays (TB5) | **£1,699** |
| **8** | **Mac Studio** | **Creator (BEST FIT)** | M5 Max (18-core CPU: 6 super + 12 performance, 32-core GPU, 16-core NPU, 460 GB/s) | 36 GB | 512 GB | None (Headless workstation) | Front: 2× USB-C, SDXC; Back: 4× Thunderbolt 5, 2× USB-A, HDMI 2.1, 10Gb Ethernet, 3.5mm jack | Mains powered; dual-fan thermal system | Up to five external displays | **£2,499** |

---

### 2. Role Recommendations & Decision Tradeoffs

#### Role 1: Travel-Heavy General User
* **Best Fit: MacBook Air 13-inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD) — £1,299**
  * *Why:* Extremely lightweight (1.24 kg / 2.7 lbs), fanless and silent, up to 18 hours battery life, 500-nit Liquid Retina display, and native dual external display support.
  * *Tradeoffs:* Lacks an internal fan (throttles slightly under prolonged heavy compute) and has only two Thunderbolt ports without built-in HDMI or SD card reader.
* **Fallback Options:**
  * *MacBook Air 15-inch (M5, £1,499):* Larger display canvas and 6-speaker audio, but heavier (1.51 kg) and bulkier on plane/train tray tables.
  * *MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, £699):* Substantially lower cost, but limited to lighter workloads, smaller display, and 1 external screen.

#### Role 2: Software Developer
* **Best Fit: MacBook Pro 14-inch (M5 Pro, 24 GB RAM, 1 TB SSD, Space Black) — £2,499**

### 2. Role Recommendations & Decision Tradeoffs

#### Role 1: Travel-Heavy General User
* **Best Fit: MacBook Air 13-inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD) — £1,299**
  * *Why:* Extremely lightweight (1.24 kg / 2.7 lbs), fanless and silent, up to 18 hours battery life, 500-nit Liquid Retina display, and native dual external display support.
  * *Tradeoffs:* Lacks an internal fan (throttles slightly under prolonged heavy compute) and has only two Thunderbolt ports without built-in HDMI or SD card reader.
* **Fallback Options:**
  * *MacBook Air 15-inch (M5, £1,499):* Larger display canvas and 6-speaker audio, but heavier (1.51 kg) and bulkier on plane/train tray tables.
  * *MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, £699):* Substantially lower cost, but limited to lighter workloads, smaller display, and 1 external screen.

#### Role 2: Software Developer
* **Best Fit: MacBook Pro 14-inch (M5 Pro, 24 GB RAM, 1 TB SSD, Space Black) — £2,499**
  * *Why:* The 15-core CPU (5 super + 10 performance cores) with active cooling handles sustained builds and parallel test suites without thermal throttling; 24 GB unified memory accommodates Docker, local VMs, and multiple IDEs; three Thunderbolt 5 (120 Gb/s) ports allow connecting up to three 6K external monitors directly; 120Hz ProMotion Liquid Retina XDR screen.
  * *Tradeoffs:* Slightly heavier (1.6 kg) and more expensive than base models; power adapter is sold separately on current configurations.
* **Fallback Options:**
  * *Mac mini M5 Pro (£1,699) or M6 (£899):* Incredible desk-bound price-to-performance, but entirely lacks portability.
  * *MacBook Pro 14-inch M5 Base (£1,999):* Retains the XDR chassis and fan, but is limited to 16 GB base RAM and 2 external displays over Thunderbolt 4.

#### Role 3: Photo/Video Creator
* **Best Fit: Mac Studio (M5 Max, 36 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD) — £2,499**
  * *Why:* Workstation-class performance with 460 GB/s memory bandwidth, dual video encode engines, dual ProRes engines, 32-core GPU, and an advanced dual centrifugal cooling system designed for non-stop rendering without thermal drop-offs. Includes front-facing SDXC and USB-C ports, four rear Thunderbolt 5 ports, 10Gb Ethernet, and drive support for up to five external displays.
  * *Tradeoffs:* Headless desktop; requires dedicated external display, keyboard, and mouse.
* **Fallback Options:**
  * *MacBook Pro 16-inch M5 Pro (£2,999):* Offers mobile editing flexibility with a built-in 16.2" reference-grade XDR screen, but starts at a higher price and has lower memory bandwidth (approx. 273 GB/s vs 460 GB/s on Studio).
  * *iMac 24-inch M4 (£1,699):* Includes a sharp 4.5K screen and all peripherals in the box, but has a smaller 24-inch panel, consumer-tier M4 chip, and max 16–32 GB memory.
